rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalafallah’s book followed al-Khuli’s interpretive approach and became a prominent source of controversy among the Amin group.
rows.anchor: فقد ترسم نهج الخولي في التفسير

rows.speaker: نصر حامد أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd said he aimed to reconnect Qur’anic studies with literary and critical studies after modern conditions had separated them from heritage and its scientific methods.
rows.anchor: كتب نصر حامد أبوزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both books stirred controversy, and their authors were accused of apostasy while public opinion was mobilized against them.
rows.anchor: وصار كلٌّ من الكتابين مثارًا للجدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author places Khalafallah’s 1947 dissertation among three especially controversial Arabic books of the period; the committee rejected it and withheld his doctorate.
rows.anchor: ثلاثة كتب هي الأشد إثارة في الحياة الثقافية العربية في النصف الأول من القرن العشرين

rows.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
rows.claim: Khalafallah argues that Qur’anic narratives should be studied as religious and literary texts, not historical documents: the Qur’an usually obscures time and place, since its aim is religious and social guidance that moves hearts and minds.
rows.anchor: يشرح محمد أحمد خلف الله منهجه في دراسة القصص القرآني

rows.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
rows.claim: He says Qur’anic stories aim at admonition, not teaching history or establishing historical facts; readers should not infer what the Qur’an did not intend.
rows.anchor: ولقد قلت في الرسالة إن قصد القرآن من قصصه

rows.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
rows.claim: Khalafallah allows that some Qur’anic stories may draw on myths without compromising revelation: the Qur’an rejects myths as proof of Muhammad’s authorship, and he surveys nine occurrences of asāṭīr.
rows.anchor: ولا يرى خلف الله بأسًا فيما ذهب إليه بعض المستشرقين

rows.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
rows.claim: He treats Qur’anic narratives as parables and adduces the story of the town’s messengers and the wives of Noah and Lot as examples.
rows.anchor: يذهب خلف الله إلى أن القرآن الكريم إنما يورد هذه القصص

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi defines narrative as discourse that guides to religion, truth, and salvation; “truth” points to proofs for justice and prophethood.
rows.anchor: ينقل خلف الله رأيًا للفخر الرازي يبين فيه أغراض القصص في سياق تفسيره للآيتين

rows.speaker: توفيق الحكيم
rows.claim: Tawfiq al-Hakim recounts that some demanded the dissertation be burned before faculty and students, while others demanded Khalafallah’s dismissal.
rows.anchor: كما أشار إلى ذلك توفيق الحكيم بقوله

rows.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
rows.claim: Khalafallah defines a literary story as imagined or reshaped events, including reordered, omitted, added, or exaggerated details that transform historical figures into fictional characters.
rows.anchor: ينقل هذا المقطع لخلف الله

rows.speaker: محمد الخضر حسين
rows.claim: Khidr Husayn rejects applying that definition to Qur’anic stories: it suits human works for artistry or pleasure, whereas divine narratives are lessons, examples, and wisdom, not imaginative writing mixing truth with falsehood.
rows.anchor: ثم يرد عليه الشيخُ الخضر حسين بقوله

rows.speaker: أحمد أمين
rows.claim: Ahmad Amin’s report characterizes the dissertation as arguing that Qur’anic stories are artistic creation unconstrained by historical accuracy and that Muhammad was an artist in this sense.
rows.anchor: بدأ أحمد أمين التقرير بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls Ahmad Amin’s report severe and inflammatory, says it catered to official religious opinion and public taste, and attributes a major role in the dissertation’s rejection to it.
rows.anchor: وكان لهذا التقرير أثر كبير في رفض لجنة المناقشة للرسالة

rows.speaker: أمين الخولي
rows.claim: Al-Khuli stood by and praised Khalafallah after the doctorate was withheld; in the third-edition preface he said public prejudice had punished the thesis, which later became a rich contribution to Qur’anic inimitability, and commended its author’s sincerity.
rows.anchor: لم يشأ الشيخ أمين الخولي التنصل من اجتهاد تلميذه

rows.speaker: أمين الخولي
rows.claim: Al-Khuli said he would declare Khalafallah’s thesis true even if no one else in Egypt or the East supported it, accepting the threat of being cast into the fire to clear his conscience.
rows.anchor: كان إصرار أمين الخولي في الدفاع عن تلميذه

rows.speaker: طه حسين
rows.claim: Taha Hussein had earlier argued that Abraham and Ishmael’s appearance in the Torah and Qur’an does not by itself establish their historical existence.
rows.anchor: طه حسين قد سبق خلف الله

rows.speaker: محمد عبده
rows.claim: Muhammad Abduh held that Qur’anic stories serve admonition rather than history or belief in every ancient report; they recount good and bad beliefs, traditions, and customs so the narrative’s form can signal approval or condemnation.
rows.anchor: وقبل طه حسين تحدث الشيخ محمد عبده عن أغراض القصص القرآني فقال

rows.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
rows.claim: To defend his approach, Khalafallah says Muhammad Abduh had already advanced it and cites al-Manar’s account of stories as lessons and signs of God’s ways, not detailed histories of peoples or places.
rows.anchor: بل سبقه إليه الشيخ محمد عبده كما ورد في تفسير المنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some writers rejected Khalafallah’s attribution of this position to Muhammad Abduh and Rashid Rida, accusing him of ignorance and misunderstanding.
rows.anchor: لم يقبل عدة كتاب ما نسبه خلف الله لمحمد عبده

rows.speaker: محمد إقبال
rows.claim: Iqbal reads Adam’s descent as an account of humanity’s moral development from instinctual desire to awareness of a free self capable of doubt and disobedience, not the appearance of the first human on earth.
rows.anchor: وفات خلف الله أن يذكر موقف محمد إقبال

rows.speaker: محمد أحمد خلف الله
rows.claim: Khalafallah calls for reading sacred narratives through the symbolic meaning of the language of religion: their purpose is guidance, not a historical account.
rows.anchor: في النصف الأول من القرن الماضي يدعو خلف الله إلى إعادة النظر في التعاطي مع لغة القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this approach remains largely rejected: Qur’anic studies still rely on inherited sciences and interpretive rules shaped by past worldviews, without opening to modern human and social sciences that al-Khuli urged scholars to use.
rows.anchor: إلا أن هذه الدعوة ما زالت غير مقبولة حتى اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book pioneered a new concept of religious language in Qur’anic studies, yet scholars, including al-Khuli’s students, remained wary; Aisha Abd al-Rahman did not follow its path and stayed within a closed, repetitive historical approach.
rows.anchor: كان كتاب «الفن القصصي في القرآن الكريم» منعطفًا رائدًا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author presents Aisha Abd al-Rahman, known as Bint al-Shati, as the finest portraitist of al-Khuli the human in her dedication to him.
rows.anchor: أجمل من يرسم صورة أمين الخولي «الإنسان» هي تلميذته

rows.speaker: عائشة عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: In that dedication, Bint al-Shati describes al-Khuli as embodying human grandeur and frailty, and says he sharpened her sense of humanity’s story from its beginning to its end.
rows.anchor: عائشة عبد الرحمن المعروفة ببنت الشاطئ، في الشهادة التي كتبتها لإهداء كتابها «القرآن وقضايا الإنسان» إليه؛ إذ تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author locates revival and reform efforts within religious schools and seminaries in Egypt, Tunisia, and Najaf, which hosted prominent figures who challenged customary ideas.
rows.anchor: انطلقت محاولات إحياء وإصلاح وتجديد تستحق الدراسة في عالم الإسلام من معاهد التعليم الديني والحواضر والحوزات المتخصصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reformers differed in the kinds, range, and depth of questions they raised, as well as in their talents and intellectual formation.
rows.anchor: وكان غيرُ واحدٍ من هؤلاء الأعلام عنوانًا للضجة في عصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They shared a rejection of uncritical reverence for heritage, a willingness to critique inherited views, and an effort to interpret texts in light of present realities and recognize the historical limits of theology and jurisprudence.
rows.anchor: يتفق هؤلاء في خروجِهم على خطاب تبجيل وتمجيد كل شيء في التراث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most reform efforts still used traditional concepts and tools; few drew on modern philosophy or human and social sciences, so they missed heritage’s hidden systems of meaning and often produced only partial interpretations and rulings.
rows.anchor: غير أن معظم هذه المحاولات على الرغم من جرأتها وأهميتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khuli was born in 1895 and died in 1966, memorized the Qur’an by age ten, studied at the School of Sharia Judiciary, and began teaching there in 1920.
rows.anchor: ولد الشيخ أمين الخولي في ١ مايو ١٨٩٥م بمحافظة المنوفية بمصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His career included service as an Egyptian imam in Rome, work in Berlin, Arabic teaching at the Egyptian University, founding the Amin group and Al-Adab magazine, and membership in Cairo’s Arabic Language Academy; the author lists several of his books.
rows.anchor: وأصبح عضوًا في مجمع اللغة العربية بالقاهرة عام ١٩٦٦م

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though he had not studied at al-Azhar, al-Khuli taught there after returning from Germany; his lectures on the history of moral philosophy were the first philosophy taught officially in the institution’s modern era.
rows.anchor: ومع أن الشيخ أمين الخولي لم يدرس في الأزهر

rows.speaker: أمين الخولي
rows.claim: Al-Khuli sought to renew rhetoric and Arabic expression by freeing them from formal logic, connecting style to life and aesthetic taste, using modern knowledge, and examining rhetoric’s psychological dimensions and interpretive context.
rows.anchor: اهتم بتجديد البلاغة وأساليب البيان العربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author characterizes al-Khuli as the first Muslim religious scholar to move from inherited methods to modern tools for building an alternative understanding of religion and criticizing older interpretations.
rows.anchor: كان الشيخ الخولي أول رجل دين مسلم حاول العبور من المناهج والمفاهيم والأدوات التراثية في فهم الدين ونصوصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The School of Sharia Judiciary combined religious subjects such as theology, jurisprudence, tafsir, and hadith with mathematics, natural sciences, history, geography, and law.
rows.anchor: المقررات التعليمية في مدرسة القضاء الشرعي يدرس التلميذ فيها معارف الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khuli spent two years in Italy, learned Italian, and studied European religious and cultural life and orientalists; he then worked in Berlin, learned German, and returned to Egypt for academic posts.
rows.anchor: وبقي في إيطاليا عامَيْن، وأجاد الإيطالية

rows.speaker: أمين الخولي
rows.claim: Exposure to European education and the Vatican’s religious teaching convinced al-Khuli that al-Azhar needed educational reform; he published his Message of al-Azhar in the Twentieth Century in 1936, and it was soon reprinted.
rows.anchor: اكتشف مدة إقامته في إيطاليا الأساليب الجديدة

rows.speaker: أمين الخولي
rows.claim: In the early 1950s, al-Khuli used a three-month newspaper series to argue for al-Azhar’s social mission, a renewed relation between religion and life, spiritual and ethical growth, and social reform.
rows.anchor: وقد أفردت جريدة المصري حينذاك مساحةً لأمين الخولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Azhar Scholars Front answered his reform campaign with a statement accusing critics of seeking status by attacking al-Azhar and its scholars.
rows.anchor: فأصدرت جبهة علماء الأزهر بيانًا ورد فيه

rows.speaker: أمين الخولي
rows.claim: Al-Khuli accused his opponents of impure motives and of monopolizing religion and divine guidance; al-Azhar issued a further response, but he continued advocating reform.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الشيخ الخولي وجه لهم نقدًا صريحًا

rows.speaker: أمين الخولي
rows.claim: Al-Khuli advocated a humane faith marked by noble feeling and cooperation, free from coercive religious authority and from a clerical class claiming to monopolize access to God.
rows.anchor: تنبه الشيخ الخولي إلى ضرورة تبني نمط «تدين

rows.speaker: أمين الخولي
rows.claim: He held that religious renewal depends on exchange with human knowledge and ways of organizing life, and that religion’s survival depends on its ability to adapt, interact, and benefit from them.
rows.anchor: لبث الشيخ الخولي كل حياته وفيًّا لتجديد الفكر الديني
